Why do we build mainly above ground instead of mainly underground?
Underground is wet, dark, and smells funny...kinda like a crazy ex-girlfriend.
I would imagine the fact that humans require sunlight and vitamin D are part of it, but regarding structure and stuff like that I don't know.
There are some types of lamps that will do just fine!

Because of the sunlight which is kind of important and because it is cheaper. If you build stuff underground you need air supplies if you build above ground you don't need that most of the time. You also have to deal with groundwater. And you can't build as deep as you can build up because at some point the stone is getting to solid and it is too much of an effort to go deeper.
It was a while before reliable shovels were created, I think at that point it was just too late to turn back.

Building underground requires that you excavate. This, depending on the property, could mean that you cut into an area, where existing electric/plumbing must be abated. The structural considerations become a greater component. Building above ground allows some leeway, in the sense of a structure of equal internal space, will require less materials and math to create.

The real reason, to absurdly simplify, is that the atmosphere is easier to hold up, than dirt and rock.
Water and moisture intrusion is one of the larger challanges. Also the backfill has to be moved somewhere.
The view isn't as nice from underground windows.
We have 4k TV's now no need for windows.
I believe it is just easier to to build above ground. Also who would want to have to use fake lighting all the time? I for one enjoy the sun :)

Costs less:

  • Don't need to pay for land excavation
  • Windows reduce lighting requirements
  • Construction materials are easier to transport
  • Less weather-based delays
  • It would require specialized laborers and training
  • The costs increase exponentially the deeper you go (substantially more than building higher would)
Because you'd need to spend alot of cash on ventilation systems to bring fresh air underground

Probably because it's easier. However there are always exceptions, for example in Coober Pedy in South Australia it's so bloody hot most of the year that most locals live underground in caves that were used to excavate opals.

The main drawback is the cost of earth removal. It's just more cost effective to build up, at least it is at this time. Some people speculate that as surface real estate becomes more and more pricey in extremely dense places like Tokyo, it will become more cost effective to build underground and the city will start expanding downward and not just up and out. Building underground has some natural benefits too, it's easier to maintain a constant temperature down there due to the insulation of the surrounding earth, ie it's cool in the summer and it's warm in the winter, it's also very naturally quiet. Most of the big downsides of underground spaces have already been addressed, lighting is easy to do with LED or fluorescents and many people in my own home city of Toronto don't even realize they have gone under ground when they pass through parts of the path system. It just feels like you're in a mall. There's a MASSIVE food court at the Eaton Centre that is entirely underground and it doesn't feel underground at all, it's open, well lit and bustling with people eating food.

As for the worries about Vitamin D deficiency from lack of sunlight and poor sleep regulation from lack of regular night and day light cycle: at one point in my life I attended a certain Canadian University at which every building on the entire campus is connected by underground tunnels. For my first year there, while I lived in residence, I used the tunnels all the time. During winter there were periods where I never went outside ONCE for months at a time and it was fucking glorious. I honestly wish I could live that way again. Canadian winters are harsh and not having to get a big jacket, hat, mitts and boots on to go to class was very convenient. Not arriving at class with snot dripping from your nose and snow all over you was like a dream come true. During that period of my life I was quite a happy individual. I'm not gonna say it's for everyone, some people do indeed need the sun but I for one was pretty happy without it for a little while and living through that convinced me that humanity could easily live underground for reasonably long periods of time and be happy if the facilities were adequately designed and engineered.
